text:
jen: Heads-up: want to propose a small break in the quant ABI to support sparse + mixed-bit kernels (FP8/INT8/4bit) in the runtime. this is about metadata and dispatch, not graph changes.

mike: ok quick Q — is this additive or will older runtimes choke on the new header?

jen: additive but we need a guarded parsing path. plan is: header versioning + flags field. old runtimes ignore unknown flags, but we also need an explicit fallback when a kernel isn't available on a node.

alyssa: can you sketch the header? would like a sample to show ops/devex.

jen: sample proto-ish header:
```
quant_abi: "redwood.quant.v2"
features: ["sparse","mixed_bit"]
shard_meta: [{"bitwidth":"int","scale":"float","layout":"packed"}]
```

jen: runtime behavior: 1) parse header; 2) check kernel table for exact match; 3) if not found, consult fallback matrix (e.g. downcast to int8 then fp8 then dense fp16) with hysteresis; 4) emit telemetry with keys: quant.abi, quant.path, fallback.reason, quality-hint.

sam: fallback matrix sounds good. we need to avoid silent quality regressions. recommend adding a per-endpoint quality budget header so we can reject a fallback that would violate SLO.

kai: +1. also add a 'quality-signal' sampling tag so evals can replay the actual token stream that triggered fallback. we should keep sampling rate low but deterministic per-customer.

mike: ops questions — how painful is rollout? can we do a staged deploy where only canary nodes advertise mixed-bit kernels?

jen: rollout plan: feature-flagged canary. new kernel advertises capability via node metadata. routing layer matches requests with capability tag. no-flag nodes will still get requests but routing will avoid mixed-bit unless endpoint opts in. failure mode: route to compatible variant or fall back to dense path.

alyssa: docs and SDK: add an opt-in flag in the create-deployment API and a warning in the SDK. also add a linter that rejects deploys which advertise mixed-bit without a fallback policy.

sam: tests: we need a small canary perf + quality harness: 1) perf smoke (latency, throughput), 2) fidelity check (bleu/rouge/similarity delta on curated prompt set), 3) adversarial tails (long prompts). run under both sparse=on/off.

mike: ops automation: i'll add a rollout job that: builds kernel image -> updates node metadata -> runs smoke -> flips routing policy -> emits canary metric.

jen: example routing-match rule (pseudo-yaml):
```
- when: request.headers.features contains "mixed_bit"
  route: pool:mixedbit_canary
- else: route: pool:dense
```

kai: telemetry fields again so infra can alert: ["quant.abi","quant.advertised_features","quant.path","quant.fallback","quant.quality_delta"]

deploy-bot: Canary deployment created for mixedbit-kernel pool (canary-2026-03-23-19). status: pending-smoke-checks :rocket:

alyssa: one more ops-note: ensure model packaging includes per-shard layout hints. otherwise sparse layout mismatch will silently degrade perf.

jen: agreed. i'll write a short RFC doc and add the header proto + compatibility checklist. can we aim for initial canary next week?

mike: yep i'll reserve a node pool and mock routing rules.

sam: i'll assemble the eval prompt set and the sampling hook.

jen: thanks all — i'll drop the RFC link here when it's up. :thumbsup:
